competition.name: DOE GEMS Prize Challenge (DrivenData competition 306)
competition.metric: Deep Fault Detection Index (DTI), alpha=0.2 beta=0.8 R=300 m
competition.known_scoring_rule: known USGS/INGENIOUS fault pixels are masked out of evaluation (DrivenData staff, forum thread 11516)

hypothesis: The competition catalogue of fault pixels is Selected At Random given terrain covariates (SAR), not SCAR: a fault's chance of being labelled, e(x)=P(s=1|y=1,x), depends on terrain x. Therefore a propensity-aware risk (Bekker & Davis 2018 Definition 2) that reweights labelled examples by 1/e(x) recovers faults in LOW-propensity terrain that the catalogue systematically omits, and a belief transform f(1-e)/(1-f e) should place more mass on unmapped-but-present faults than an nnPU baseline that assumes selection is random.
mechanism: Documented, not assumed: Giddens & Faulds 2025 (SGP-TR-229) report only ~25% of the Great Basin study area is mapped at 1:24,000 and state that step-overs along range-front faults are over-represented because steep topographic gradients make them easier to identify; Faulds 2026 (51st Workshop) reports lidar now covers much of the region while detailed maps still cover <25%. Selection therefore favours high-relief, range-front, well-expressed terrain and disfavours basin-floor/alluvium-covered and quadrangle-boundary structures. Implementation: propensity design = [1, z(5 covariates), z(4 continuous)^2] over relief, slope, gravity-derived basin-fill proxy, lidar coverage, distance to range front (a strictly smaller attribute set than the classifier's, per arXiv:1809.03207 sec 5.1); classifier = 48-feature random-Fourier-feature logistic on all 23 features; arm A = Definition-2 propensity-weighted ERM with weights clipped at 10; arm B = nnPU (Kiryo 2017) with pi from a Horvitz-Thompson estimate 1/mean(1/e) of the SAME anchored propensity; belief = f(1-e)/(1-f e); emission = Poisson-disk greedy, min distance 2.8 px, >=3 px catalogue buffer, 38,000 dots.

mimic_process.name: alluvial and eolian burial of basin floors
mimic_process.why_it_mimics: Post-faulting sediment cover produces exactly the covariate signature the hypothesis treats as 'present but unmapped': low relief, low curvature variance, low lidar-derived scarp density, large gravity-derived basin-fill. A model keyed only on 'flat and blank' scores on buried alluvium, which contains fewer faults per unit area than mapped uplands simply because it is younger surface.
mimic_process.control_used: every candidate pairs a suppression term (why it was not mapped) with a presence term (why a fault is physically there: strand-pair geometry, basement-depth discontinuity, seismic-velocity or strain-rate anomaly). The leakage canary also bounds it: no single covariate reaches AUC 0.90 on the holdout (max measured 0.5738 over 28 features), so no covariate is a disguised copy of the label.

holdout_dti.evidence_class: HOLDOUT-DTI (proxy truth = withheld segments of the given catalogue)
holdout_dti.cell_design: 4 quadrant blocks x 2 draws, spatially blocked, identical folds for both arms
holdout_dti.gate_rule: higher blocked-holdout pooled DTI overall AND no loss in the highest-propensity tercile

instrument_validity.interpretation: the blocked holdout is ANTI-correlated with owner-reported live scores across the registry corpus, because live scoring masks known-fault pixels while this holdout's truth IS catalogue pixels. The gate is therefore respected but is not evidence about live performance (IR-65-006).

holdout_dti.not_a_projection: no live score is projected anywhere in this repo; every number is either a holdout measurement, an instrument measurement, or an owner-reported receipt.

registry_comparison.protocol_thresholds: lane drift if rank-correlation > 0.90 with any registry raster, or > 70% of dots within 3 px of one registry raster's dots
registry_comparison.caveat: the first build reported max rho 0.9743, which was a tie-breaking bug in the shared dupcheck helper, not real drift; fixed with scipy rankdata and locked by tests/test_dupcheck.py (IR-65-003).

irregularities.title: Propensity scale is not identifiable from PU data, and no reachable public index of exhaustively mapped quadrangles exists
Template holdout eligibility dilation did not reach the withheld truth (shared-tool bug, fixed in the template pattern)
Duplicate-check Spearman used positional tie-breaking, so every pair of submission rasters looked correlated (rho ~ 0.97)
EM initialisation deviated from the paper and produced a degenerate fixed point
Two conflicting 'highest leaderboard score' values in the standing brief, neither verifiable from this sandbox
The catalogue-hidden holdout structurally cannot reward the lane's own thesis
Data are restored from an owner-supplied GitHub mirror, not from DrivenData
EM convergence diagnostic was mislabelled: the logged 'll' was only the f-part of the complete-data likelihood
